messages.subject: Spatio-temporal model specification
parts:
Dear all,

I'm using a similar model for my spatio-temporal data to the one in the Cameletti et al. (2012) paper. In the paper, the mesh is constructed so that each data location has a dedicated mesh node and the matrix B in eq. 12 is used to select the data indices from the node indices. However, for my data, I have constructed the mesh so that not all if any of the observations have the same location as the mesh nodes and there are fewer nodes than the data locations. In this case, how is the model specified exactly?

Thanks

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatio-temporal model specification
parts:
On 18/03/13 16:11, Jussi wrote:
> I'm using a similar model for my spatio-temporal data to the one in
> the Cameletti et al. (2012) paper. In the paper, the mesh is
> constructed so that each data location has a dedicated mesh node and
> the matrix B in eq. 12 is used to select the data indices from the
> node indices. However, for my data, I have constructed the mesh so
> that not all if any of the observations have the same location as the
> mesh nodes and there are fewer nodes than the data locations. In this
> case, how is the model specified exactly?

Hi,

while the paper happens to use a mesh such that all observation points
are nodes in the mesh, the code in the paper does not actually depend on
that, but instead uses the more general idea that each row of the B
matrix (A.est in the code in the paper) contains interpolation weights
within a triangle. For the mesh in the paper those weights happen to be
just zeros and a single "1".
Thus you should be able to simply follow the same code as in the paper.

Finn
